### Introduction

Sun-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) is a re-emitted signal directly originating from the photosynthetic system, representing plant fluorescence observed from space. It is therefore considered a direct measure of plant physiological status and responses to environmental changes, while also serving as a potential indicator for estimating global gross primary productivity (GPP). However, the revisit cycles and operational altitudes of existing SIF observation platforms limit their spatio-temporal resolution. This results in decoupling between the linear relationship between global-scale SIF and GPP at finer temporal and spatial scales.
The Sentinel-5P TROPOMI sensor, with its daily nadir spatial resolution of 3.5 × 5.5-7 km, enables more detailed observation of SIF/GPP in terrestrial ecosystems. The following example illustrates the downscaling process (i.e., increasing the spatial resolution) for SIF based on an mechanistic model that relates SIF with land-surface temperature, and NIRv (a vegetation index).

### Libraries
We will need the following libraries to run the downscaling processor
```{python}
import openeo
import rioxarray as rio

"""
Currently there is an issue with openEO back-end that doesnt allow us to upsample datacubes (For more details see [here](https://forum.dataspace.copernicus.eu/t/how-to-spatial-upsampling-when-using-resample-cube-spatial/4358/6)). For this reason we will need some other libraries to process the parameters cube locally, perform a spatial upsample, create a stac catalog and publish the file and catalog on github.
This is needed to create a STAC item for the upsampled parameters:
"""
import pystac
from pystac.extensions.projection import ProjectionExtension
from pystac.extensions.eo import EOExtension
from datetime import datetime
from shapely.geometry import box, mapping
import json
import subprocess

# For data visualization
import xarray as xr
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# For spatial resampling
import xesmf as xe
import xarray_regrid
import numpy as np
```

## Study number 1: Downscaling SIF in the Iberian peninsula

### Area of Interest and Time Period

Before going into the details of the datasets, we need to define an area of interest and time period for our analysis. For this example, we will focus on the Iberian Peninsula during the time period between 2023-07-17 and 2023-07-23.

```{python}
spatial_extent_prototype = {
    "west": -10.0,
    "east": 0.0,
    "south": 35.0,
    "north": 45.0,
}

temporal_extent_prototype = ["2023-07-17", "2023-07-21"]
```

```{python}
# | echo: false
import cartopy.crs as ccrs
import cartopy.feature as cfeature
from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle


def plot_world_with_bbox(bbox, title="World Map with Bounding Box"):
    """
    Plot world map with a bounding box overlay.

    Parameters:
    -----------
    bbox : tuple or list
        Bounding box coordinates as (min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat)
    title : str
        Plot title
    """
    min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat = (
        bbox["west"],
        bbox["south"],
        bbox["east"],
        bbox["north"],
    )

    # Create figure and axis with PlateCarree projection
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(
        figsize=(15, 10), subplot_kw={"projection": ccrs.PlateCarree()}
    )

    # Add map features
    ax.add_feature(cfeature.LAND, facecolor="lightgray", edgecolor="none")
    ax.add_feature(cfeature.OCEAN, facecolor="lightblue")
    ax.add_feature(cfeature.COASTLINE, linewidth=0.5)
    ax.add_feature(cfeature.BORDERS, linewidth=0.3, linestyle=":")
    ax.add_feature(
        cfeature.LAKES, facecolor="lightblue", edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.3
    )

    # Add gridlines
    gl = ax.gridlines(
        draw_labels=True, linewidth=0.5, color="gray", alpha=0.5, linestyle="--"
    )
    gl.top_labels = False
    gl.right_labels = False

    # Set global extent
    ax.set_global()

    # Draw bounding box
    width = max_lon - min_lon
    height = max_lat - min_lat

    bbox_patch = Rectangle(
        (min_lon, min_lat),
        width,
        height,
        linewidth=2,
        edgecolor="red",
        facecolor="none",
        transform=ccrs.PlateCarree(),
        zorder=5,
    )
    ax.add_patch(bbox_patch)

    # Add a label for the bbox
    center_lon = (min_lon + max_lon) / 2
    center_lat = (min_lat + max_lat) / 2
    ax.text(
        center_lon,
        max_lat + 5,
        "Area of Interest",
        transform=ccrs.PlateCarree(),
        ha="center",
        fontsize=10,
        color="red",
        weight="bold",
    )

    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=14, weight="bold", pad=20)

    plt.tight_layout()
    return fig, ax


fig1, ax1 = plot_world_with_bbox(spatial_extent_prototype, " ")

plt.show()

```

```{python}
connection = openeo.connect(
```

### Variables

For this tutorial we will use the following datasets/variables:

Target:

| Variable name | Collection | Band Name | Spatial resolution|
|--|--|--|--|
|Sun-Induced Flourescence| [Dong Li SIF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dpabon/SIF_downscaling_CDSE/refs/heads/main/data/SIF_20180629.json)| ```SIF```| 5 km |

Currently there are two SIF gridded products derived from Sentinel-5p that are availables:

1. [S5P-PAL SIF](https://data-portal.s5p-pal.com/products/troposif.html). This product is generated by the Sentinel-5P Product Algorithm Laboratory (S5P-PAL) and contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data processed by S[&]T. Unfortunately, the current (at least at: 2025-12-01) STAC dissemination only include plain netcdf files and not cloud optimized data format. Currently the [Atmosphere Virtual Lab project](https://atmospherevirtuallab.org/) is working in provided zarr datacubes for the L3 products, including SIF.

2. [Dong LI SIF](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0034425725003918#da0005). This product uses an artificial neural network to retrieve SIF from Sentinel-5p observations. Thanks to Dong Li for provinding us with a [gridded example of the product](https://github.com/dpabon/SIF_downscaling_CDSE/blob/main/data/SIF_20180629.tif) and the [stac item](https://github.com/dpabon/SIF_downscaling_CDSE/blob/main/data/SIF_20180629.json) necessary to ingest the product in the openEO-CDSE infrastructure. This files can be found in the data directory of the [repository](https://github.com/dpabon/SIF_downscaling_CDSE).

Predictors:

| Variable name | Collection | Band Name | Spatial resolution |
|--|--|--|--|
|Land Surface Temperature| ```SENTINEL3_SLSTR_L2_LST```| ```LST```| 1 km|
|Near Infrared Vegetation Index| ```SENTINEL3_OLCI_L2_LAND```| ```RC681```, ```RC865```| 300 m|
: SIF predictors {#tbl-predictors}

#### Creating openEO datacubes for the variables

```{python}
# Testing SIF - Dong Li

cube_SIF_original_median = connection.load_stac(
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dpabon/SIF_downscaling_CDSE/refs/heads/main/data/2023-07-SIF/5_days_composites/SIF_20230717_20230721.json",

    temporal_extent=temporal_extent_prototype,

```


```{python}



cube_LST = connection.load_collection(
    "SENTINEL3_SLSTR_L2_LST",
    spatial_extent=spatial_extent_prototype,
    temporal_extent=temporal_extent_prototype,
    bands=["LST"],
)

cube_LST_qc = connection.load_collection(
    "SENTINEL3_SLSTR_L2_LST",
    spatial_extent=spatial_extent_prototype,
    temporal_extent=temporal_extent_prototype,
    bands=["confidence_in"],
)

red = connection.load_collection(
    "SENTINEL3_OLCI_L2_LAND",
    spatial_extent=spatial_extent_prototype,
    temporal_extent=temporal_extent_prototype,
    bands=["RC681"],
)

nir = connection.load_collection(
    "SENTINEL3_OLCI_L2_LAND",
    spatial_extent=spatial_extent_prototype,
    temporal_extent=temporal_extent_prototype,
    bands=["RC865"],
)

cube_NIRv = ((nir - red) / (nir + red)) * nir

cube_NIRv = cube_NIRv.rename_labels(dimension="bands", target=["NIRv"])

cube_OLCI_qc = connection.load_collection(
    "SENTINEL3_OLCI_L2_LAND",
    spatial_extent=spatial_extent_prototype,
    temporal_extent=temporal_extent_prototype,
    bands=["LQSF"],
)

```

For this analysis we will compute a composite of the area of interest using all the observations during the time period for all the variables except SIF that is already one time step observation.

```{python}

cube_NIRv_median = cube_NIRv_masked.reduce_temporal(reducer="median")

```

### SIF parameter optimization at low spatial resolution

To predict SIF we use the following formulation:

::: {#def-sif}
$$SIF = f(V) \cdot f(T)$$
:::

where $f(V)$ represents the vegetation module and $V$ is a vegation index: 
$$f(V) = b_2 \cdot V^{b_1}$$


$f(T)$ represents the temperature module where $T$ is a variable that represent temperature stress (e.g. air temperature at 2 meters, or land surface temperature)

$$
f(T) = e^{-\frac{(T + b_5)^2}{2b_6^2}}
$$


Given the previous formulation we optimize the function using L-BFGS-B and a spatial moving window with 40 observations. The optimization function is defined in [udf_parameters_optim_low_res.py](https://github.com/dpabon/SIF_downscaling_CDSE/blob/main/sif_downscaling_openEO_CDSE/udf/udf_parameters_optim_low_res.py).

First we need to define the boundaries and start values for $b1$, $b2$, $b5$ $b6$ parameters:

```{python}
# the order for each variable follows: b1,b2,b3,b4,b5,b6

param_min = [0, 0.1, -310, 1]

param_ini = [1, 2, -295, 20]

param_max = [1.5, 5, -290, 50]
```


To apply the optimization function in the data cube we define an openEO User Define Function using:

```{python}
my_udf = openeo.UDF.from_file(
    "src/udf/udf_parameters_optim_low_res.py",
    context={
        "param_ini": param_ini,
        "param_min": param_min,
        "param_max": param_max,
        "min_obs": 40,
        "window_size_lat": 7,
        "window_size_lon": 7,
    },
)

```

Notice that the size of the moving window is set using ```window_size_lat``` and ```window_size_lon```.

Then we can apply our function to the data cube using:
```{python}

parameters_cube_low = dataset_SIF_low.apply_neighborhood(
    process=my_udf,
    size=[
        {"dimension": "x", "value": 512, "unit": "px"},
        {"dimension": "y", "value": 512, "unit": "px"},
    ],
    overlap=[
        {"dimension": "x", "value": 20, "unit": "px"},
        {"dimension": "y", "value": 20, "unit": "px"},
    ],
)

# changing the name of the ouput
output_bands = ["b1", "b2", "b5", "b6"]

parameters_cube_low_rename = parameters_cube_low.rename_labels("bands", output_bands)

```

and see the process graph:
```{python}
parameters_cube_low_rename
```

Now we will download the cube the optimized parameters to have a look and spatially upsample to match the Sentinel-3 cube at high resolution.

### Upsampling the parameters cube

::: {.callout-note}

Until openEO team solve the upsampling issue. For details see [CDSE discusion forum](https://forum.dataspace.copernicus.eu/t/how-to-spatial-upsampling-when-using-resample-cube-spatial/4358/6) We need to make a workaround to upsample the parameters cube.

:::

This is a temporary solution
```{python}
# | code-fold: true
# | eval: false

parameters_low = rio.open_rasterio("data/results_parameters_optim_low_resolution_iberian_peninsula.tif")

parameters_low = parameters_low.drop_vars("spatial_ref")


# LST high resolution local
nirv_high = rio.open_rasterio("data/cube_nirv_1km_mask_iberian_peninsula.tif")

nirv_high = nirv_high.drop_vars(["spatial_ref", "band"])



parameters_high = parameters_low.regrid.conservative(nirv_high)

parameters_high_2 = xr.DataArray(parameters_high.data.todense(), coords=parameters_high.coords)

# Saving the resample raster

parameters_high_2.rio.to_raster("data/results_paramaters_high_resolution_iberian_peninsula.tif")

# plotting results
# plt.clf()
fig, axs = plt.subplots(nrows=2, ncols=2, figsize=(8, 6))
axs = axs.flatten()
counter = 0
for i in [1, 2, 5, 6]:
    parameters_high_2.isel(band=counter).plot(ax=axs[counter])
    axs[counter].set_title(f"b{i}")
    counter += 1

plt.tight_layout()

```

::: {.callout-important}
Change the following path accordindly to your github repository.
:::

```{python}
# | code-fold: true
# | eval: false

output_path = "https://github.com/dpabon/SIF_downscaling_CDSE/raw/refs/heads/main/data/results_paramaters_high_resolution_iberian_peninsula.tif"
```

```{python}
# | code-fold: true
# | eval: false

# Get metadata from the raster
bbox = list(parameters_high.rio.bounds())  # [minx, miny, maxx, maxy]
epsg = "4326"
shape = [parameters_high.rio.height, parameters_high.rio.width]

# Create geometry from bbox
geom = mapping(box(*bbox))

# Create the STAC item
item = pystac.Item(
    id="results_parameters_high_resolution",
    geometry=geom,
    bbox=bbox,
    datetime=datetime.strptime(temporal_extent_prototype[0], "%Y-%m-%d"),
    properties={},
)

# Add projection extension
proj_ext = ProjectionExtension.ext(item, add_if_missing=True)
proj_ext.epsg = epsg
proj_ext.shape = shape
proj_ext.bbox = bbox

# Add EO extension
EOExtension.ext(item, add_if_missing=True)

# Add the asset
item.add_asset(
    key="parameters",
    asset=pystac.Asset(
        href=output_path,  # or use an absolute path / URL
        title="Optimized Parameters High Resolution",
        media_type="image/tiff; application=geotiff",
        extra_fields={"eo:bands": [{"name": f"b{i}"} for i in [1, 2, 5, 6]]},
    ),
)


# Save as JSON

with open("data/results_parameters_high_resolution_iberian_peninsula.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(item.to_dict(), f, indent=2)

print(item.to_dict())

# pushing changes to the remote repo to access from openEO again

git_commit = ["git", "commit", "-m", '"Upsampling of parameters updated"', "data/results_paramaters_high_resolution_iberian_peninsula.tif", "data/results_parameters_high_resolution_iberian_peninsula.json"]

subprocess.run(git_commit)

git_push = ["git", "push"]

subprocess.run(git_push)

# plotting the resampled parameters

fig, axs = plt.subplots(nrows=2, ncols=2, figsize=(8, 8))
axs = axs.flatten()

for i in range(4):
    parameters_high.sel(band=i + 1).plot(ax=axs[i])
    axs[i].set_title(f"b{i + 1}")

plt.tight_layout()

```

### Downscaling SIF

To downscale SIF we will use @def-sif. The code implementation of @def-sif is available at [udf_sif_downscaling.py](https://github.com/dpabon/SIF_downscaling_CDSE/blob/main/sif_downscaling_openEO_CDSE/udf/udf_sif_downscaling.py). Then we can call the ```udf``` using:


```{python}
udf_sif_prediction = openeo.UDF.from_file(
    "src/udf/udf_sif_downscaling.py",
    context={"window_size_lat": 3, "window_size_lon": 3},
)

sif_downscaled = cube_to_upscale.apply_neighborhood(
    udf_sif_prediction,
    size=[
        {"dimension": "x", "value": 512, "unit": "px"},
        {"dimension": "y", "value": 512, "unit": "px"},
    ],
    overlap=[
        {"dimension": "x", "value": 20, "unit": "px"},
        {"dimension": "y", "value": 20, "unit": "px"},
    ],
)
```



It is not possible to reduce the number of bands using ```apply_neighborhood``` then we need to just select the first band:

```{python}
# removing bands that are not needed it

sif_downscaled_renamed = sif_downscaled.rename_labels(
    dimension="bands", source=["b1"], target=["SIF"]
)

sif_downscaled_renamed = sif_downscaled_renamed.band("SIF")
```

Now we can run everthing and save the results

```{python}
)
"""
```

```{python}
# | echo: false
import cartopy.crs as ccrs
import cartopy.feature as cfeature
from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle


def plot_world_with_bbox(bbox, title="World Map with Bounding Box"):
    """
    Plot world map with a bounding box overlay.

    Parameters:
    -----------
    bbox : tuple or list
        Bounding box coordinates as (min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat)
    title : str
        Plot title
    """
    min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat = (
        bbox["west"],
        bbox["south"],
        bbox["east"],
        bbox["north"],
    )

    # Create figure and axis with PlateCarree projection
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(
        figsize=(15, 10), subplot_kw={"projection": ccrs.PlateCarree()}
    )

    # Add map features
    ax.add_feature(cfeature.LAND, facecolor="lightgray", edgecolor="none")
    ax.add_feature(cfeature.OCEAN, facecolor="lightblue")
    ax.add_feature(cfeature.COASTLINE, linewidth=0.5)
    ax.add_feature(cfeature.BORDERS, linewidth=0.3, linestyle=":")
    ax.add_feature(
        cfeature.LAKES, facecolor="lightblue", edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.3
    )

    # Add gridlines
    gl = ax.gridlines(
        draw_labels=True, linewidth=0.5, color="gray", alpha=0.5, linestyle="--"
    )
    gl.top_labels = False
    gl.right_labels = False

    # Set global extent
    ax.set_global()

    # Draw bounding box
    width = max_lon - min_lon
    height = max_lat - min_lat

    bbox_patch = Rectangle(
        (min_lon, min_lat),
        width,
        height,
        linewidth=2,
        edgecolor="red",
        facecolor="none",
        transform=ccrs.PlateCarree(),
        zorder=5,
    )
    ax.add_patch(bbox_patch)

    # Add a label for the bbox
    center_lon = (min_lon + max_lon) / 2
    center_lat = (min_lat + max_lat) / 2
    ax.text(
        center_lon,
        max_lat + 5,
        "Area of Interest",
        transform=ccrs.PlateCarree(),
        ha="center",
        fontsize=10,
        color="red",
        weight="bold",
    )

    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=14, weight="bold", pad=20)

    plt.tight_layout()
    return fig, ax


fig1, ax1 = plot_world_with_bbox(spatial_extent_prototype, " ")

plt.show()

```

### Variables

For this tutorial we will use the following datasets/variables:

Target:

| Variable name | Collection | Band Name | Spatial resolution|
|--|--|--|--|
|Sun-Induced Flourescence| [Dong Li SIF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dpabon/SIF_downscaling_CDSE/refs/heads/main/data/SIF_20180629.json)| ```SIF```| 5 km |

Currently there are two SIF gridded products derived from Sentinel-5p that are availables:

1. [S5P-PAL SIF](https://data-portal.s5p-pal.com/products/troposif.html). This product is generated by the Sentinel-5P Product Algorithm Laboratory (S5P-PAL) and contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data processed by S[&]T. Unfortunately, the current (at least at: 2025-12-01) STAC dissemination only include plain netcdf files and not cloud optimized data format. Currently the [Atmosphere Virtual Lab project](https://atmospherevirtuallab.org/) is working in provided zarr datacubes for the L3 products, including SIF.

2. [Dong LI SIF](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0034425725003918#da0005). This product uses an artificial neural network to retrieve SIF from Sentinel-5p observations. Thanks to Dong Li for provinding us with a [gridded example of the product](https://github.com/dpabon/SIF_downscaling_CDSE/blob/main/data/SIF_20180629.tif) and the [stac item](https://github.com/dpabon/SIF_downscaling_CDSE/blob/main/data/SIF_20180629.json) necessary to ingest the product in the openEO-CDSE infrastructure. This files can be found in the data directory of the [repository](https://github.com/dpabon/SIF_downscaling_CDSE).

Predictors:

| Variable name | Collection | Band Name | Spatial resolution |
|--|--|--|--|
|Land Surface Temperature| ```SENTINEL3_SLSTR_L2_LST```| ```LST```| 1 km|
|Near Infrared Vegetation Index| ```SENTINEL3_OLCI_L2_LAND```| ```RC681```, ```RC865```| 300 m|
: SIF predictors {#tbl-predictors}

### SIF parameter optimization at low spatial resolution

To predict SIF we use the following formulation:

::: {#def-sif}
$$SIF = f(V) \cdot f(T)$$
:::

where $f(V)$ represents the vegetation module and $V$ is a vegation index: 
$$f(V) = b_2 \cdot V^{b_1}$$


$f(T)$ represents the temperature module where $T$ is a variable that represent temperature stress (e.g. air temperature at 2 meters, or land surface temperature)

$$
f(T) = e^{-\frac{(T + b_5)^2}{2b_6^2}}
$$


Given the previous formulation we optimize the function using L-BFGS-B and a spatial moving window with 40 observations. The optimization function is defined in [udf_parameters_optim_low_res.py](https://github.com/dpabon/SIF_downscaling_CDSE/blob/main/sif_downscaling_openEO_CDSE/udf/udf_parameters_optim_low_res.py).

First we need to define the boundaries and start values for $b1$, $b2$, $b5$ $b6$ parameters:

```{python}
# the order for each variable follows: b1,b2,b3,b4,b5,b6

param_min = [0, 0.1, -310, 1]

param_ini = [1, 2, -295, 20]

param_max = [1.5, 5, -290, 50]
```


To apply the optimization function in the data cube we define an openEO User Define Function using:

```{python}
my_udf = openeo.UDF.from_file(
    "src/udf/udf_parameters_optim_low_res.py",
    context={
        "param_ini": param_ini,
        "param_min": param_min,
        "param_max": param_max,
        "min_obs": 40,
        "window_size_lat": 7,
        "window_size_lon": 7,
    },
)

```

Notice that the size of the moving window is set using ```window_size_lat``` and ```window_size_lon```.

Then we can apply our function to the data cube using:
```{python}

parameters_cube_low = dataset_SIF_low.apply_neighborhood(
    process=my_udf,
    size=[
        {"dimension": "x", "value": 512, "unit": "px"},
        {"dimension": "y", "value": 512, "unit": "px"},
    ],
    overlap=[
        {"dimension": "x", "value": 20, "unit": "px"},
        {"dimension": "y", "value": 20, "unit": "px"},
    ],
)

# changing the name of the ouput
output_bands = ["b1", "b2", "b5", "b6"]

parameters_cube_low_rename = parameters_cube_low.rename_labels("bands", output_bands)

```

and see the process graph:
```{python}
parameters_cube_low_rename
```

### Upsampling the parameters cube

::: {.callout-note}

Until openEO team solve the upsampling issue. For details see [CDSE discusion forum](https://forum.dataspace.copernicus.eu/t/how-to-spatial-upsampling-when-using-resample-cube-spatial/4358/6) We need to make a workaround to upsample the parameters cube.

:::

This is a temporary solution
```{python}
# | code-fold: true
# | eval: false

parameters_low = rio.open_rasterio("data/results_parameters_optim_low_resolution_indonesia_example.tif")

parameters_low = parameters_low.drop_vars("spatial_ref")


# LST high resolution local
nirv_high = rio.open_rasterio("data/cube_nirv_1km_mask_indonesia_example.tif")

nirv_high = nirv_high.drop_vars(["spatial_ref", "band"])



parameters_high = parameters_low.regrid.conservative(nirv_high)

parameters_high_2 = xr.DataArray(parameters_high.data.todense(), coords=parameters_high.coords)

# Saving the resample raster

parameters_high_2.rio.to_raster("data/results_paramaters_high_resolution_indonesia_example.tif")

# plotting results
# plt.clf()
fig, axs = plt.subplots(nrows=2, ncols=2, figsize=(8, 6))
axs = axs.flatten()
counter = 0
for i in [1, 2, 5, 6]:
    parameters_high_2.isel(band=counter).plot(ax=axs[counter])
    axs[counter].set_title(f"b{i}")
    counter += 1

plt.tight_layout()

```

::: {.callout-important}
Change the following path accordindly to your github repository.
:::

```{python}
# | code-fold: true
# | eval: false

output_path = "https://github.com/dpabon/SIF_downscaling_CDSE/raw/refs/heads/main/data/results_paramaters_high_resolution_indonesia_example.tif"
```

```{python}
# | code-fold: true
# | eval: false

# Get metadata from the raster
bbox = list(parameters_high.rio.bounds())  # [minx, miny, maxx, maxy]
epsg = "4326"
shape = [parameters_high.rio.height, parameters_high.rio.width]

# Create geometry from bbox
geom = mapping(box(*bbox))

# Create the STAC item
item = pystac.Item(
    id="results_parameters_high_resolution",
    geometry=geom,
    bbox=bbox,
    datetime=datetime.strptime(temporal_extent_prototype[0], "%Y-%m-%d"),
    properties={},
)

# Add projection extension
proj_ext = ProjectionExtension.ext(item, add_if_missing=True)
proj_ext.epsg = epsg
proj_ext.shape = shape
proj_ext.bbox = bbox

# Add EO extension
EOExtension.ext(item, add_if_missing=True)

# Add the asset
item.add_asset(
    key="parameters",
    asset=pystac.Asset(
        href=output_path,  # or use an absolute path / URL
        title="Optimized Parameters High Resolution",
        media_type="image/tiff; application=geotiff",
        extra_fields={"eo:bands": [{"name": f"b{i}"} for i in [1, 2, 5, 6]]},
    ),
)


# Save as JSON

with open("data/results_parameters_high_resolution_indonesia_example.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(item.to_dict(), f, indent=2)

print(item.to_dict())

# pushing changes to the remote repo to access from openEO again

git_commit = ["git", "commit", "-m", '"Upsampling of parameters updated"', "data/results_paramaters_high_resolution_indonesia_example.tif", "data/results_parameters_high_resolution_indonesia_example.json"]

subprocess.run(git_commit)

git_push = ["git", "push"]
```

### Downscaling SIF

To downscale SIF we will use @def-sif. The code implementation of @def-sif is available at [udf_sif_downscaling.py](https://github.com/dpabon/SIF_downscaling_CDSE/blob/main/sif_downscaling_openEO_CDSE/udf/udf_sif_downscaling.py). Then we can call the ```udf``` using:


```{python}
udf_sif_prediction = openeo.UDF.from_file(
    "src/udf/udf_sif_downscaling.py",
    context={"window_size_lat": 3, "window_size_lon": 3},
)

sif_downscaled = cube_to_upscale.apply_neighborhood(
    udf_sif_prediction,
    size=[
        {"dimension": "x", "value": 512, "unit": "px"},
        {"dimension": "y", "value": 512, "unit": "px"},
    ],
    overlap=[
        {"dimension": "x", "value": 20, "unit": "px"},
        {"dimension": "y", "value": 20, "unit": "px"},
    ],
)
```



It is not possible to reduce the number of bands using ```apply_neighborhood``` then we need to just select the first band:

```{python}
# removing bands that are not needed it

sif_downscaled_renamed = sif_downscaled.rename_labels(
    dimension="bands", source=["b1"], target=["SIF"]
)

sif_downscaled_renamed = sif_downscaled_renamed.band("SIF")
```

```{python}
)
"""
```

## Study number 3: Downscaling dcSIF (8-day, 0.05°) in the Pannonian Basin

This study applies the same workflow to a third region and replaces the SIF input with a different gridded product: daily-corrected SIF (dcSIF) as an 8-day composite at 0.05°. The processing chain (masking, compositing, resampling, parameter optimization, upsampling workaround and prediction) is the same as in the previous studies.

| | Study 1 and 2 | Study 3 |
|--|--|--|
| SIF input | Dong Li SIF, 5-day composite, 0.1° | dcSIF, 8-day composite, 0.05° |
| Region | Iberian Peninsula / Indonesia | Pannonian Basin (Hungary and surroundings) |
| Time window | 5 days | 2023-07-20 to 2023-07-27 |
: Differences between Study 3 and the previous studies {#tbl-study3-differences}

### Area of Interest and Time Period

```{python}
spatial_extent_prototype = {
    "west": 16.0,
    "east": 23.0,
    "south": 45.5,
    "north": 48.5,
}

# The end date is exclusive in openEO: "2023-07-28" covers the full 8-day window.
temporal_extent_prototype = ["2023-07-20", "2023-07-28"]
```

```{python}
# | echo: false
fig1, ax1 = plot_world_with_bbox(spatial_extent_prototype, " ")
plt.show()
```

### Variables

Target:

| Variable name | Source | Band Name | Spatial resolution | Temporal resolution |
|--|--|--|--|--|
| Sun-Induced Fluorescence, day-length corrected (dcSIF) | TROPOMI, gridded | ```SIF``` | 0.05° | 8 days |
: dcSIF target {#tbl-study3-target}

The dcSIF product ([Deng et al., 2026; doi:10.5281/zenodo.22766916](https://zenodo.org/records/22766916)) provides day length corrected global SIF from TROPOMI at 0.05° and 8-day resolution (May 2018 – July 2025). The input Level-2 soundings are retrieved with the artificial neural network approach of [Li et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2025.114987) and aggregated onto a regular grid with the oversampling approach of Frankenberg et al., as implemented in [SatelliteGridding.jl](https://github.com/cfranken/SatelliteGridding). The day-length correction follows [Köhler et al. (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1029/2018GL079031). The 8-day windows start on 1 January of each year; the window used here (2023-07-20 to 2023-07-27) is time step 26 of 2023. The predictors are the same as in the previous studies (@tbl-predictors).

#### Preparing dcSIF for openEO

The dcSIF product is distributed on Zenodo as one NetCDF file per year (dimensions `lat`, `lon`, `time`; variable `sif_dc`). `load_stac` cannot read these files directly: it needs a raster file at a public URL described by a STAC item. The script [convert_dcsif_to_stac.py](https://github.com/dpabon/SIF_downscaling_CDSE/blob/main/src/convert_dcsif_to_stac.py) prepares the input used in this study. It:

1. downloads the yearly NetCDF file from [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/22766916) (`TROPOMI_ANN_dcSIF_0d05deg_8day_2023.nc`, about 1.2 GB) to a folder outside the repository and checks its MD5 checksum;
2. extracts the 8-day time step starting on 2023-07-20 and crops it to the area of interest plus a 1° margin;
3. writes it as a Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF (`EPSG:4326`, north-up, nodata −9999);
4. creates a STAC item with the same structure as the other items in the `data` directory (`datetime` at the centre of the 8-day window, band `SIF` declared in `eo:bands`).

The resulting files are `data/2023-07-dcSIF/dcSIF_8day_20230720_20230727_pannonian_basin.tif` and `.json`. To prepare another time step or region, change `YEAR`, `WINDOW_START`, `REGION` and `spatial_extent` at the top of the script and run it from the repository root:

```bash
python src/convert_dcsif_to_stac.py
```

For this time step, dcSIF is available for all grid cells of the area of interest (median 0.64; 1st and 99th percentiles 0.31 and 0.89). The parameter bounds of the previous studies are kept.

#### Creating openEO datacubes for the variables

::: {.callout-note}
The preflight validation of the openEO back-end sometimes fails with `CollectionNotFound` for `SENTINEL3_SLSTR_L2_LST` or `SENTINEL3_OLCI_L2_LAND`, although both collections exist. This is intermittent: resubmitting the job, or connecting directly to the CDSE back-end (`https://openeo.dataspace.copernicus.eu/`), solves it.
:::

```{python}
cube_SIF_original_median = connection.load_stac(
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dpabon/SIF_downscaling_CDSE/refs/heads/main/data/2023-07-dcSIF/dcSIF_8day_20230720_20230727_pannonian_basin.json",
    bands=["SIF"],
    spatial_extent=spatial_extent_prototype,
    temporal_extent=temporal_extent_prototype,
)

cube_LST = connection.load_collection(
    "SENTINEL3_SLSTR_L2_LST",
    spatial_extent=spatial_extent_prototype,
    temporal_extent=temporal_extent_prototype,
    bands=["LST"],
)

cube_LST_qc = connection.load_collection(
    "SENTINEL3_SLSTR_L2_LST",
    spatial_extent=spatial_extent_prototype,
    temporal_extent=temporal_extent_prototype,
    bands=["confidence_in"],
)

red = connection.load_collection(
    "SENTINEL3_OLCI_L2_LAND",
    spatial_extent=spatial_extent_prototype,
    temporal_extent=temporal_extent_prototype,
    bands=["RC681"],
)

nir = connection.load_collection(
    "SENTINEL3_OLCI_L2_LAND",
    spatial_extent=spatial_extent_prototype,
    temporal_extent=temporal_extent_prototype,
    bands=["RC865"],
)

cube_NIRv = ((nir - red) / (nir + red)) * nir

cube_NIRv = cube_NIRv.rename_labels(dimension="bands", target=["NIRv"])

cube_OLCI_qc = connection.load_collection(
    "SENTINEL3_OLCI_L2_LAND",
    spatial_extent=spatial_extent_prototype,
    temporal_extent=temporal_extent_prototype,
    bands=["LQSF"],
)
```

#### Masking clouds, reducing the time dimension and resampling OLCI at 1 km

```{python}
cube_LST_masked = cube_LST.mask(cube_LST_qc > 5000)
cube_NIRv_masked = cube_NIRv.mask(cube_OLCI_qc > 10000)

cube_LST_median = cube_LST_masked.reduce_temporal(reducer="max")
cube_NIRv_median = cube_NIRv_masked.reduce_temporal(reducer="median")

cube_NIRv_median_1 = cube_NIRv_median.resample_cube_spatial(
    target=cube_LST_median, method="med"
)
```

### SIF parameter optimization at low spatial resolution

We use the same formulation (@def-sif), parameter bounds and optimization function as in the previous studies:

```{python}
param_min = [0, 0.1, -310, 1]
param_ini = [1, 2, -295, 20]
param_max = [1.5, 5, -290, 50]

my_udf = openeo.UDF.from_file(
    "src/udf/udf_parameters_optim_low_res.py",
    context={
        "param_ini": param_ini,
        "param_min": param_min,
        "param_max": param_max,
        "min_obs": 40,
        "window_size_lat": 7,
        "window_size_lon": 7,
    },
)

parameters_cube_low = dataset_SIF_low.apply_neighborhood(
    process=my_udf,
    size=[
        {"dimension": "x", "value": 512, "unit": "px"},
        {"dimension": "y", "value": 512, "unit": "px"},
    ],
    overlap=[
        {"dimension": "x", "value": 20, "unit": "px"},
        {"dimension": "y", "value": 20, "unit": "px"},
    ],
)

parameters_cube_low_rename = parameters_cube_low.rename_labels(
    "bands", ["b1", "b2", "b5", "b6"]
)
```

With `window_size_lat = window_size_lon = 7` the moving window is 15 × 15 grid cells, i.e. 0.75° on the 0.05° dcSIF grid instead of 1.5° on the 0.1° grid of Study 1 and 2.

### Upsampling the parameters cube

Same workaround as in the previous studies: the parameters are upsampled locally to the 1 km NIRv grid, published with a STAC item, and loaded again with `load_stac`.

```{python}
# | code-fold: true
# | eval: false

parameters_low = rio.open_rasterio(
    "data/results_parameters_optim_low_resolution_pannonian_basin_dcsif.tif"
).drop_vars("spatial_ref")

nirv_high = rio.open_rasterio("data/cube_nirv_1km_mask_pannonian_basin_dcsif.tif")
nirv_high = nirv_high.drop_vars(["spatial_ref", "band"])

parameters_high = parameters_low.regrid.conservative(nirv_high)

data_high = parameters_high.data
if hasattr(data_high, "todense"):
    data_high = data_high.todense()

parameters_high_2 = xr.DataArray(
    data_high, coords=parameters_high.coords, dims=parameters_high.dims
)
parameters_high_2 = parameters_high_2.rio.write_crs("EPSG:4326")
parameters_high_2.rio.to_raster(
    "data/results_paramaters_high_resolution_pannonian_basin_dcsif.tif"
)
```

::: {.callout-important}
Change the following path accordingly to your github repository.
:::

```{python}
# | code-fold: true
# | eval: false

output_path = "https://github.com/dpabon/SIF_downscaling_CDSE/raw/refs/heads/main/data/results_paramaters_high_resolution_pannonian_basin_dcsif.tif"

bbox = list(parameters_high_2.rio.bounds())
shape = [parameters_high_2.rio.height, parameters_high_2.rio.width]

item = pystac.Item(
    id="results_parameters_high_resolution_pannonian_basin_dcsif",
    geometry=mapping(box(*bbox)),
    bbox=bbox,
    datetime=datetime.strptime(temporal_extent_prototype[0], "%Y-%m-%d"),
    properties={},
)

proj_ext = ProjectionExtension.ext(item, add_if_missing=True)
proj_ext.epsg = 4326
proj_ext.shape = shape
proj_ext.bbox = bbox

EOExtension.ext(item, add_if_missing=True)

item.add_asset(
    key="parameters",
    asset=pystac.Asset(
        href=output_path,
        title="Optimized Parameters High Resolution",
        media_type="image/tiff; application=geotiff",
        extra_fields={"eo:bands": [{"name": f"b{i}"} for i in [1, 2, 5, 6]]},
    ),
)

with open("data/results_parameters_high_resolution_pannonian_basin_dcsif.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(item.to_dict(), f, indent=2)

# New files need to be added before they can be committed
files = [
    "data/results_paramaters_high_resolution_pannonian_basin_dcsif.tif",
    "data/results_parameters_high_resolution_pannonian_basin_dcsif.json",
]
subprocess.run(["git", "add", *files], check=True)
subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-m", "Upsampled parameters Pannonian Basin dcSIF", *files], check=True)
subprocess.run(["git", "push"], check=True)
```

```{python}
# | eval: false
sif_downscaled_renamed.execute_batch(
    outputfile="data/openeo_sif_downscaled_pannonian_basin_dcsif.tif",
    title="SIF_downscaling",
    description="Predicting SIF at high spatial resolution",
)
```

### Comparing SIF products

```{python}
sif_downscaled_local = rio.open_rasterio("data/openeo_sif_downscaled_pannonian_basin_dcsif.tif")

# Same colour bar for both products
sif_vmax = float(np.nanpercentile(cube_sif_local.values, 99))

fig, axs = plt.subplots(nrows=2, figsize=(8, 11))
cube_sif_local.plot(ax=axs[0], vmin=0, vmax=sif_vmax)
axs[0].set_title("dcSIF (0.05°, original)")
sif_downscaled_local.plot(ax=axs[1], vmin=0, vmax=sif_vmax)
axs[1].set_title("SIF (1 km, downscaled)")
plt.tight_layout()
```

To check the downscaling, we aggregate the downscaled SIF back to the original dcSIF grid:

```{python}
# | eval: false
sif_downscaled_resampled = sif_downscaled_renamed.resample_cube_spatial(
    target=cube_SIF_original_median, method="med"
)
sif_downscaled_resampled.execute_batch(
    outputfile="data/sif_downscaled_resampled_pannonian_basin_dcsif.tif"
)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
The batch job above re-runs the whole processing chain before aggregating. The same aggregation can be done locally from the downloaded 1 km result:

```python
from rasterio.enums import Resampling

sif_ds = rio.open_rasterio(
    "data/openeo_sif_downscaled_pannonian_basin_dcsif.tif", masked=True
).squeeze().rio.write_nodata(np.nan)
sif_ds_res = sif_ds.rio.reproject_match(cube_sif_local.squeeze(), resampling=Resampling.average)
sif_ds_res.rio.to_raster("data/sif_downscaled_resampled_pannonian_basin_dcsif.tif")
```
:::

Comparing the original SIF with the downscaled SIF + spatial resampling, with summary statistics over the cells valid in both:

```{python}
sif_orig = cube_sif_local.squeeze()
sif_agg = rio.open_rasterio(
    "data/sif_downscaled_resampled_pannonian_basin_dcsif.tif", mask_and_scale=True
).squeeze()
sif_agg = sif_agg.rio.reproject_match(sif_orig)

both = (sif_orig.notnull() & sif_agg.notnull()).values
o = sif_orig.values[both]
d = sif_agg.values[both]
print(f"Common valid cells: {both.sum()}")
print(f"Bias (original - aggregated): {np.mean(o - d):.3f}")
print(f"RMSE: {np.sqrt(np.mean((o - d) ** 2)):.3f}")
print(f"Pearson r: {np.corrcoef(o, d)[0, 1]:.3f}")
```

```{python}
fig, axs = plt.subplots(nrows=2, figsize=(6, 10))
sif_orig.plot(ax=axs[0], vmin=0, vmax=sif_vmax)
axs[0].set_title("dcSIF (Original)")
sif_agg.plot(ax=axs[1], vmin=0, vmax=sif_vmax)
axs[1].set_title("SIF (Downscaled) resampled")

plt.tight_layout()
```

Now we can compare the original SIF with the downscaled SIF + spatial resampling using $originalSIF - upscaledSIF$

```{python}
fig, axs = plt.subplots(nrows=1, figsize=(6, 6))
differences = sif_orig - sif_agg
differences.plot()
```
